title: Stainless steel: grain-aware cleaning and polishing
audience: Cleaners who service stainless steel appliances, lift doors, sinks and fountains in offices, commercial buildings and residences.
learningOutcomes: Tell a brushed stainless steel surface from a polished one and choose the method that suits it.
Clean stainless steel with the grain, starting with the gentlest method and stepping up only as needed.
Apply a polish evenly, then buff it off without leaving marks.

instruction.heading: Why stainless steel needs its own method
instruction.body: Stainless steel withstands corrosion and rust, which makes it a common choice for appliances, lift doors, sinks and water fountains. Its protective layer depends on the surface being kept clean. Fingerprints, food films, and hard-water deposits left on the surface can dull it or start discolouration if they are not removed. The main risk is not the soil itself but the damage done while removing it, which is why the method should start gently and only step up when needed.

instruction.heading: Find the finish and the grain
instruction.body: Stainless steel has several finishes. The one most often met in buildings is a brushed finish, which shows fine lines running in one direction. Those lines are the grain. A polished finish looks more like a mirror and shows marks more clearly. Before you start, run your eye along the surface in a low light and find the line of the grain. Every wipe, including the final buff, should follow that direction. Wiping across the grain leaves fine scratches that stay visible.

instruction.heading: Start gently: glass cleaner first
instruction.body: For light soil, use glass cleaner on a blue cloth and move along the grain until the metal is dry. Work across the whole surface before you move on. A lint-free cloth gives the best finish and does not leave fibres behind. Stop here if the surface is clean.

instruction.heading: Step up: mild detergent, then polish
instruction.body: For tougher soil, dilute a gentle detergent of near-neutral pH, roughly 7 to 8, in a spray bottle according to the maker's instructions. Dampen a cloth with it rather than soaking the metal, and wipe along the grain. Dry straight away with a second dry microfiber cloth, still moving with the grain. Only once the metal is dry should polish go on. Put a small amount on a clean cloth, work it along the grain with light overlapping strokes, and check that the film is even. Follow the polish label for the amount and how long to leave it before buffing.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection before you start.
Identify the finish and find the line of the grain under a low light.
Apply glass cleaner on a blue cloth and move along the grain until the steel dries. Repeat across the whole area.
If soil remains, make up a mild detergent to the maker's instructions and dampen a yellow cloth with it.
Move along the grain, then dry at once with a clean, dry microfiber cloth, also following the grain.
Once dry, put a small amount of polish on a clean cloth as the label directs and work it along the grain.
Buff off the polish with a clean dry cloth, following the grain, and check for an even finish.

workedExamples.situation: A brushed stainless steel lift door has fingerprints and a faint film. The cleaner wipes in circles with a damp cloth and the surface now shows swirls.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the error, and what should be done to correct the surface?
workedExamples.reasoning: Circular wiping cuts across the brushed grain and leaves swirls. Starting again with glass cleaner and wiping with the grain, then drying and buffing in the same direction, should reduce the swirl marks. If marks remain, the supervisor should check whether the finish can be restored with the approved product.

workedExamples.situation: A polished stainless steel sink has water spots after rinsing. The cleaner wants to use a stronger product to remove them quickly.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the right next step?
workedExamples.reasoning: Start with the gentlest method, glass cleaner with the grain, and dry straight away. Water spots are often removed by drying promptly, so a stronger product is not needed. Only step up to a mild detergent if the gentler method fails.

equipmentAndPpe: Glass cleaner suitable for stainless steel.
Gentle detergent of near-neutral pH, mixed to the label.
Colour-coded microfiber cloths, one set reserved for stainless steel.
Stainless steel polish, only where the site product list allows it.

commonErrors.error: Wiping in circles, or across the grain, which leaves visible scratches.
commonErrors.prevention: Find the grain first and wipe, dry and buff in one direction.

commonErrors.error: Applying polish to a wet surface, so it smears or dilutes.
commonErrors.prevention: Dry the surface completely before applying polish.

commonErrors.error: Using a scourer or an abrasive pad to remove a mark.
commonErrors.prevention: Start with glass cleaner or mild detergent, and ask the supervisor before using anything stronger.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wear gloves and eye protection when spraying cleaners or polish. Keep sprays away from your eyes.
Do not mix detergents with other chemicals. Check labels before use, and follow the product's own dilution directions.

qualityStandard: The surface is clean with no fingerprints or film visible under normal lighting.
All wiping, drying and buffing marks run along the grain.
Polish, where applied, is even and fully buffed off with no smears.
No scratches or new marks are visible after the job.
documentationEvidence: Job record of the stainless steel surfaces cleaned, and the method used for each.
Note of any surface with scratches or marks that were not present before, for supervisor review.
summary: Find the grain before you start, and keep every stroke with it.
Start with glass cleaner, step up to a mild detergent only if needed, and dry at once.
Apply polish only to a dry surface, then buff it off with the grain.
Do not use scourers or abrasives on stainless steel.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which direction should the cloth move on a brushed stainless steel surface?
options: Moving in loose circles, so that the whole surface is covered quickly
With the grain, so that the strokes match the lines of the finish
Across the grain, so that the surface is scrubbed more firmly

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct order for cleaning stainless steel?
options: Polish first to lift the soil, then a stronger product and then glass cleaner
Abrasive pad first, then glass cleaner to finish and then polish the whole surface
Glass cleaner first, then a mild detergent if needed, then polish on a dry surface

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the surface be fully dry before a polish for stainless steel is applied?
options: Because a wet surface can smear or dilute the polish so that it cannot buff evenly
Because polish only works on cold metal and it smears on warm surfaces
Because the polish needs water to bind to the steel and the steel must be wet first
